concepts.title: Purpose of Note-making
concepts.definition: Note-making distils a long text into brief personal pointers for one's own later reference -- not a copy, but a skeleton of main points and supporting details that lets the note-maker reconstruct the substance without rereading everything.
concepts.key_idea: Notes are written for yourself -- short, structured signals that unlock the full text in memory.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb111.txt opening (why note making, for one's own reference, i know what i want to say but not how to say it)

solution_steps.explain: Notes serve the note-maker alone, so brevity and personal shorthand are legitimate.
Sort each sentence into main points and supporting evidence before writing anything down.
Test the notes: a month later they should rebuild the text's argument without the original.

concepts.title: Mechanics: Abbreviations, Headings and Layout
concepts.definition: Effective notes use an indented layout with a clear title, main headings, sub-points and sub-sub-points, sparing abbreviations and symbols, and numbered or lettered indentation so hierarchy is visible at a glance.
concepts.key_idea: Indentation shows importance -- the further in a point sits, the more it depends on the point above.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb111.txt mechanics sections (title, abbreviations and symbols, indentation, headings and sub points, numbering)
question_patterns: describe the correct layout for making notes

solution_steps.explain: A short title announces the passage's subject and frames every point below.
Main points sit flush left; sub-points and sub-sub-points indent successively with numbers or letters.
Standard abbreviations and symbols shrink the text while keeping each entry readable.

concepts.title: From Notes to Meaning: Avoiding Copying
concepts.definition: The commonest fault is transcribing sentences instead of making notes. Genuine note-making translates the author's prose into compressed phrasing -- phrases, not sentences -- discarding examples and repetition, so the notes show the shape of the argument rather than its original wording.
concepts.key_idea: Notes compress and translate; copying merely relocates -- the difference is thinking.
concepts.textbook_ref: kehb111.txt guidance sections (do not copy, use phrases, discard examples and repetition, notes versus summary distinction)

solution_steps.explain: Strip articles and verbs of full clauses; keep the idea in a noun phrase.
Drop illustrations, repetitions and asides that elaborate but do not advance the argument.
Retain the order and weight of the original reasoning so notes mirror the passage's logic.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A student's notes read: 'The passage is about how trees give us many things such as wood, fruits and shade and therefore we should not cut them down.' Diagnose the faults and rewrite.

solution_template.explain: The entry is a full copied sentence -- not a note.
Title: Uses of trees. 1. give wood, fruit, shade 2. must not be cut.
Headings, indentation and compressed phrases now follow the standard layout.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Distinguish note-making from summarising using the same short passage on trees.

solution_template.explain: Indented phrases under a title -- for the maker's own reference.
A short linked paragraph in complete sentences -- meant to be shown to others.
Notes are private, skeletal and ungrammatical by design; summaries are public and grammatical.
